item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: Two-thirds of the people present at the beginning of a meeting are men. Nobody leaves but 10 more men and 10 more women arrive at the meeting. Which of the following statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: There would then be more men than women at the meeting.

options.label: B
options.text: There would then be the same number of men as there are women at the meeting.

options.label: C
options.text: There would then be more women than men at the meeting.

options.label: D
options.text: From the information given, you cannot tell whether there would be more women or men.

item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Sophie has a bag in which there are 16 marbles: 8 are red and 8 are black marbles. She draws 2 marbles from the bag and does not put them back. Both marbles are black. She then draws a third marble out of the bag. What can you say about the likely color of this third marble?

options.label: A
options.text: It is more likely to be red than black.

options.label: B
options.text: It is more likely to be black than red.

options.label: C
options.text: It is equally likely to be red or black.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot tell if red or black is more likely.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the distribution of crops grown in a certain country.

[Image: Pie chart showing the distribution of crops]

According to the information in the graph, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: More oats are grown than wheat.

options.label: B
options.text: Corn is more than one-half of the country’s crop.

options.label: C
options.text: Oats are more than one-third of the country’s crop.

options.label: D
options.text: The total crop of oats and wheat is greater than the corn crop.

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing four sectors labeled with crop types:
- 'Corn': occupies slightly less than half of the circle, spanning from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to approximately the 4:30 position (roughly 135° to 140°).
- 'Oats': adjacent clockwise from Corn, spanning from approximately 4:30 to 7 o'clock (roughly 75°).
- 'Other': adjacent clockwise from Oats, spanning from approximately 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock (roughly 30°).
- 'Wheat': adjacent clockwise from Other to Corn, spanning from approximately 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (roughly 115° to 120°).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
The smaller box contains 20 tickets numbered from 1 to 20. The larger box contains 100 tickets numbered from 1 to 100.

[Image: Two boxes containing tickets]

Without looking at them, you can pick a ticket from either box. Which box would give you the greater chance of picking out a ticket with the number 17 on it?

options.label: B
options.text: The box with 100 tickets

options.label: C
options.text: Both boxes would give the same chance

options.label: D

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The results of a long jump competition were reported as follows:

| | Average Length |
| --- | --- |
| Team A | 3.6 m |
| Team B | 4.8 m |

There were the same number of students in each team.
Which statement about the competition MUST be true?

options.label: A
options.text: Each student in team B jumped farther than any student in team A.

options.label: B
options.text: After every student in team A jumped, there was a student in team B who jumped farther.

options.label: C
options.text: As a group, team B jumped farther than team A.

options.label: D
options.text: Some students in team A jumped farther than some students in team B.

reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Popularity of Subjects

A group of 10 students wanted to find out whether mathematics or history was more popular for their group. They rated each subject using the following scale.

[Image: Rating scale from 1 to 5]

The table shows the results:

Students’ Ratings

| Student | Mathematics Rating | History Rating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alan | 1 | 2 |
| Lisa | 4 | 4 |
| Ann | 5 | 4 |
| John | 2 | 2 |
| Connor | 4 | 2 |
| Georgia | 3 | 3 |
| Bret | 2 | 1 |
| Courtney | 1 | 1 |
| Ian | 5 | 3 |
| Jackson | 3 | 2 |
| Totals | 30 | 24 |

B. The students’ ratings are shown on the graph below. For example, Alan’s name is by his ratings (mathematics 1, history 2).

[Image: Scatter plot showing students' ratings]

Write True or False in the space after each of these statements:

All students in the group liked mathematics more than they liked history. ____

Nearly half of the students gave both subjects the same rating. ____

Two students neither liked nor disliked either subject. ____
